verses.original: וַיֵּ֥רַע אֶל־ יוֹנָ֖ה רָעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיִּ֖חַר לֽוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·ra‘ ’el- yō·w·nāh rā·‘āh ḡə·ḏō·w·lāh way·yi·ḥar lōw
verses.literal: Jonah, however was greatly displeased . . . . . . and he became angry
verses.literalPt: Mas isso desagradou extremamente a Jonas, e ele ficou irado.

verses.original: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל אֶל־ יְהוָ֜ה וַיֹּאמַ֗ר אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ הֲלוֹא־ זֶ֣ה דְבָרִ֗י עַד־ הֱיוֹתִי֙ עַל־ אַדְמָתִ֔י עַל־ כֵּ֥ן קִדַּ֖מְתִּי לִבְרֹ֣חַ תַּרְשִׁ֑ישָׁה כִּ֣י יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ אֵֽל־ חַנּ֣וּן וְרַח֔וּם אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֙יִם֙ וְרַב־ חֶ֔סֶד וְנִחָ֖ם עַל־ הָרָעָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiṯ·pal·lêl ’el- Yah·weh way·yō·mar ’ān·nāh Yah·weh hă·lō·w- zeh ḏə·ḇā·rî ‘aḏ- hĕ·yō·w·ṯî ‘al- ’aḏ·mā·ṯî ‘al- kên qid·dam·tî liḇ·rō·aḥ tar·šî·šāh kî yā·ḏa‘·tî kî ’at·tāh ’êl- ḥan·nūn wə·ra·ḥūm ’e·reḵ ’ap·pa·yim wə·raḇ- ḥe·seḏ wə·ni·ḥām ‘al- hā·rā·‘āh
verses.literal: So he prayed to the LORD saying O LORD is this not what I said while I was still in my own country This is why . . . I was so quick to flee toward Tarshish I knew . . . that You are a gracious and compassionate God slow to anger abounding in loving devotion One who relents from sending disaster
verses.literalPt: Orou a Jeová e disse: Ah! Jeová, não foi esta a minha palavra, estando eu ainda no meu país? Por isso é que me apressei a fugir para Társis, pois eu sabia que tu és um Deus clemente e misericordioso, tardio em irar-se e de grande beneficência e que te arrependes do mal.

verses.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה קַח־ נָ֥א אֶת־ נַפְשִׁ֖י מִמֶּ֑נִּי כִּ֛י ט֥וֹב מוֹתִ֖י מֵחַיָּֽי׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·‘at·tāh Yah·weh qaḥ- nā ’eṯ- nap̄·šî mim·men·nî kî ṭō·wḇ mō·w·ṯî mê·ḥay·yāy
verses.literal: And now O LORD please take my life from me for it is better for me to die than to live
verses.literalPt: Agora, Jeová, tira-me a vida, pois melhor me é morrer do que viver.

verses.literal: But the LORD replied Have you any right to be angry
verses.literalPt: Respondeu Jeová: Fica-te bem a tua ira?

verses.original: וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹנָה֙ מִן־ הָעִ֔יר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב מִקֶּ֣דֶם לָעִ֑יר וַיַּעַשׂ֩ ל֨וֹ שָׁ֜ם סֻכָּ֗ה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב תַּחְתֶּ֙יהָ֙ בַּצֵּ֔ל עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִרְאֶ֔ה מַה־ יִּהְיֶ֖ה בָּעִֽיר׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·ṣê yō·w·nāh min- hā·‘îr way·yê·šeḇ miq·qe·ḏem lā·‘îr way·ya·‘aś lōw šām suk·kāh way·yê·šeḇ taḥ·te·hā baṣ·ṣêl ‘aḏ ’ă·šer yir·’eh mah- yih·yeh bā·‘îr
verses.literal: Then Jonah left the city and sat down east of it . . . where he made himself a shelter and sat . . . in its shade to see what would happen to the city
verses.literalPt: Então, Jonas saiu da cidade e se assentou ao oriente dela; ali, fez para si uma barraca e, debaixo dela, sentou-se à sombra, até ver o que houvesse de suceder à cidade.

verses.original: וַיְמַ֣ן יְהוָֽה־ אֱ֠לֹהִים קִיקָי֞וֹן וַיַּ֣עַל׀ מֵעַ֣ל לְיוֹנָ֗ה לִֽהְי֥וֹת צֵל֙ עַל־ רֹאשׁ֔וֹ לְהַצִּ֥יל ל֖וֹ מֵרָֽעָת֑וֹ וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח יוֹנָ֛ה עַל־ הַקִּֽיקָי֖וֹן שִׂמְחָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·man Yah·weh- ’ĕ·lō·hîm qî·qā·yō·wn way·ya·‘al mê·‘al lə·yō·w·nāh lih·yō·wṯ ṣêl ‘al- rō·šōw lə·haṣ·ṣîl lōw mê·rā·‘ā·ṯōw way·yiś·maḥ yō·w·nāh ‘al- haq·qî·qā·yō·wn śim·ḥāh ḡə·ḏō·w·lāh
verses.literal: So the LORD God appointed a vine and it grew up to provide shade over Jonah’s head to ease his discomfort and Jonah . . . was greatly . . . pleased with the plant
verses.literalPt: Deus Jeová preparou um palma-christi e fê-lo subir por cima de Jonas, para que lhe desse sombra sobre a cabeça, a fim de o livrar do seu mau estado. Jonas, pois, ficou em extremo contente por causa do palma-christi.

verses.original: וַיְמַ֤ן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ תּוֹלַ֔עַת בַּעֲל֥וֹת הַשַּׁ֖חַר לַֽמָּחֳרָ֑ת וַתַּ֥ךְ אֶת־ הַקִּֽיקָי֖וֹן וַיִּיבָֽשׁ׃
verses.transliteration: way·man hā·’ĕ·lō·hîm tō·w·la·‘aṯ ba·‘ă·lō·wṯ haš·ša·ḥar lam·mā·ḥo·rāṯ wat·taḵ ’eṯ- haq·qî·qā·yō·wn way·yî·ḇāš
verses.literal: When dawn came the next day God appointed a worm that attacked the plant so that it withered
verses.literalPt: Deus, porém, preparou um bicho ao romper da alva no dia seguinte, e o bicho feriu o palma-christi, de sorte que se secou.

verses.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ כִּזְרֹ֣חַ הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ וַיְמַ֨ן אֱלֹהִ֜ים ר֤וּחַ קָדִים֙ חֲרִישִׁ֔ית וַתַּ֥ךְ הַשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ עַל־ רֹ֥אשׁ יוֹנָ֖ה וַיִּתְעַלָּ֑ף וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל אֶת־ נַפְשׁוֹ֙ לָמ֔וּת וַיֹּ֕אמֶר ט֥וֹב מוֹתִ֖י מֵחַיָּֽי׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî kiz·rō·aḥ haš·še·meš way·man ’ĕ·lō·hîm rū·aḥ qā·ḏîm ḥă·rî·šîṯ wat·taḵ haš·še·meš ‘al- rōš yō·w·nāh way·yiṯ·‘al·lāp̄ way·yiš·’al ’eṯ- nap̄·šōw lā·mūṯ way·yō·mer ṭō·wḇ mō·w·ṯî mê·ḥay·yāy
verses.literal: As the sun was rising God appointed a scorching east wind and the sun beat down on Jonah’s head so that he grew faint and wished to die saying It is better for me to die than to live
verses.literalPt: Ao nascer do sol, preparou Deus um vento calmoso do oriente; o sol deu na cabeça de Jonas, de maneira que desmaiou; pediu para si a morte e disse: Melhor me é morrer do que viver.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־ יוֹנָ֔ה הַהֵיטֵ֥ב חָרָֽה־ לְךָ֖ עַל־ הַקִּֽיקָי֑וֹן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֵיטֵ֥ב חָֽרָה־ לִ֖י עַד־ מָֽוֶת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ĕ·lō·hîm ’el- yō·w·nāh ha·hê·ṭêḇ ḥā·rāh- lə·ḵā ‘al- haq·qî·qā·yō·wn way·yō·mer hê·ṭêḇ ḥā·rāh- lî ‘aḏ- mā·weṯ
verses.literal: Then God . . . asked Jonah Have you any right to be angry about the plant I do he replied I am angry enough to die
verses.literalPt: Deus perguntou a Jonas: Fica-te bem a tua ira por causa do palma-christi? Respondeu ele: Tenho razão de me irar até a morte.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אַתָּ֥ה חַ֙סְתָּ֙ עַל־ הַקִּ֣יקָי֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־ עָמַ֥לְתָּ בּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֣א גִדַּלְתּ֑וֹ שֶׁבִּן־ לַ֥יְלָה הָיָ֖ה וּבִן־ לַ֥יְלָה אָבָֽד׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer Yah·weh ’at·tāh ḥas·tā ‘al- haq·qî·qā·yō·wn ’ă·šer lō- ‘ā·mal·tā bōw wə·lō ḡid·dal·tōw šeb·bin- lay·lāh hā·yāh ū·ḇin- lay·lāh ’ā·ḇāḏ
verses.literal: But the LORD said You cared about the plant which you neither tended nor made grow It sprang up in a night . . . and perished in a night . . .
verses.literalPt: Jeová disse: Tu tiveste compaixão do palma-christi, pela qual não trabalhaste, nem fizeste crescer; que nasceu numa noite e numa noite pereceu.

verses.original: וַֽאֲנִי֙ לֹ֣א אָח֔וּס עַל־ נִינְוֵ֖ה הָעִ֣יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ בָּ֡הּ הַרְבֵּה֩ מִֽשְׁתֵּים־ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה רִבּ֜וֹ אָדָ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ יָדַע֙ בֵּין־ יְמִינ֣וֹ לִשְׂמֹאל֔וֹ וּבְהֵמָ֖ה רַבָּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: wa·’ă·nî lō ’ā·ḥūs ‘al- nî·nə·wêh hā·‘îr hag·gə·ḏō·w·lāh ’ă·šer yeš- bāh har·bêh miš·têm- ‘eś·rêh rib·bōw ’ā·ḏām ’ă·šer lō- yā·ḏa‘ bên- yə·mî·nōw liś·mō·lōw ū·ḇə·hê·māh rab·bāh
verses.literal: So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh which has more than 120,000 . . . . . . people who cannot tell . . . their right hand from their left and many cattle as well
verses.literalPt: Não hei de eu ter compaixão da grande cidade de Nínive, em que há mais de cento e vinte mil pessoas que não sabem discernir entre a sua mão direita e a sua esquerda, e também muito gado?
